label: Small-characteristic finite-field DLP
problem: Discrete logarithms in finite fields of small characteristic; the practical example is the pairing field F_(2^(4*1223)), not F_(2^1223).
notes: Theoretical advances and concrete security reassessments are distinct events. We do not join leading L-indices, modular-multiplication estimates and measured runtimes on one curve. The former 2^70 placeholder is removed. No parameter-size inversion is supplied.

milestones.name: Joux subexponential algorithm
milestones.event: Heuristic L_Q(1/4+o(1)) complexity, with embeddings into a suitable extension when needed.
milestones.notes: This is subexponential, not quasi-polynomial. No numerical reference-instance estimate is assigned.

milestones.name: BGJT quasi-polynomial algorithm
milestones.event: Heuristic n^O(log n) time, where n is the field bit-size; still super-polynomial.
milestones.notes: First public preprint date; no constant for a concrete inversion is inferred.

milestones.name: Concrete reassessment of a supersingular pairing field
milestones.event: Estimated about 59 bits for DLP in F_(2^(4*1223)), in the authors’ modular-multiplication units.
milestones.notes: The curve base field is F_(2^1223). The analysis uses L(1/4)-type techniques; the BGJT elimination steps were not required. This is a concrete estimate, not an executed 59-bit computation or a cost for the base field.
